# N knights: Soar agent from the Rosie teaching script

**Runnable.** `n-knights.soar` loads the shared library (`Soar/soar-library`, v2.42) and `n-knights-rules.soar` (14 task rules, generated by `gen.py` from the statements in `english-input.txt`; `tools/rosie_chess.py`). Generated 18 Nov 2026. Needs Soar 9.6.6 (or the PyPI soar-sml bindings).

## Run

    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . n-knights.soar --seed 1 --cap 60000
    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . n-knights.soar --json | python3 ../../tools/check_moves.py n-knights init-nknights2.world

`python3 gen.py WORLD` writes the same rules with another example state as the initial world.

## Results (library v2.42, 18 Nov 2026)

Example states (`gen.py WORLD`, `run_agent.py --check`): init-nknights2: goal false, failure false; fail-nknights2: goal true, failure true; final-nknights2: goal true, failure false.

Seeds 1-3, cap 60,000 decisions; plans replayed independently by `check_moves.py` (legality from the action statements, the losing conditions, the goal).

| Seed | Outcome | Decisions | Actions | Replay |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | cap | 60,000 | 0 | goal does not hold |
| 2 | cap | 60,000 | 0 | goal does not hold |
| 3 | cap | 60,000 | 0 | goal does not hold |

## Translation

- Operator place-block (argument1 = the block, argument2 = the location), statement 5. available (statement 6) and clear
  (statement 7) are maintained one-argument relations; the blocks start in a stack (A-C2).
- A placed block has the row and column of the location it is on; the relations between blocks are static relations
  between their locations (A-C1).
- Failure: a block is jumpable by another block: the knight's move, a static relation computed as in knight
  swapping (alongside, diagonal-with, near; A-S3).
- The goal (all blocks are placed) is expanded over the blocks of the world file.
Propose initialize-n-knights when its conditions below hold.

The assumption codes (A-S, A-G, A-C, A-P) are explained in `tools/rosie_chess.py` and `../../PILOT.md`.
